question: Should OpenClaw solve memory-wiki vault isolation through generic per-agent plugin config, a memory-wiki-owned per-agent/context vault resolver, or a documented unsupported/shared-gateway limitation?
rationale: The fix changes plugin/config API surface and security-sensitive durable memory isolation semantics, and automation cannot safely choose the long-term contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a maintainer-owned per-agent plugin config merge contract and land memory-wiki as the first consumer with upgrade, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep scope inside memory-wiki
options.body: Add memory-wiki-specific per-agent or context-aware vault mapping without creating a broad plugin API, accepting a narrower solution for this plugin only.

options.title: Document shared-gateway limitation
options.body: Do not add new config/API surface now; document separate gateways or external plugins as the supported isolation path until a broader design is approved.

recommendation.title: Define generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-owned per-agent plugin config merge contract and land memory-wiki as the first consumer with upgrade, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses plugin SDK/config boundaries and security-sensitive config policy, where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
